findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of soil build-up in the dish machine. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspectors that the soil accumulation will be clean. Ensure that the accumulation is monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment:
The following plumbing repairs requirements were observed.
1. The left faucet on the triple sink was observed leaking. 
2. The faucet on the dump sink was observed leaking continuously.
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspectors that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that the plumbings is in good repair according to the LAW.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed. 
1. An accumulation of grease build up was observed on the sides of the  fryers. 
2. The coving trim tile under the drink station was observed coming off the wall. 
3. Inspectors observed a hole in the trim edge of the door to the dry storage. 
Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspectors that the areas mentioned will receive the relevant corrections. Ensure that these corrections are made to provide smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employee was observed donning gloves without washing their hands while preparing food. Discussed with PIC and employee was educated about proper handwashing procedures. Ensure that hands are washed in between tasks before changing gloves at all times during food prep.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed cheese sauce being stored in the original can after being opened. PIC was educated about potential botulism contamination and the storage of the cheese sauce was changed. Ensure that food items in cans are transfer to adequate storage to avoid potential contamination hazards.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed raw chicken being stored over fish in the two compartment cooler at the far end of the kitchen by the dish machine area. Discussed with PIC and the storage order was corrected. Ensure that the adequate storage order for food items are practice efficiently.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: Inspector observed mop to be stored on the ground by the dish machine and by the mop bucket. Hang mops sot hat they can dry. 

After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed shelf liner on shelf behind hot holding to be absorbent and not cleanable. Replace liner with a material that is consistent with the following section of the code. 

4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Observed shelves under the serving window to be soiled with flour. It was difficult to see if the shelves needed sealing as well. Seal shelves, if necessary, after cleaning.  Also the front/outside of the Over/Under refrigeration unit, next to the utility sink, is soiled. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee to wash hands correctly with warm water and soap, but turn the faucet handles off without a barrier such as a paper towel. Dry hands with paper towel after proper hand washing, then use dirty paper towel to turn off the faucet handles. Ensure all staff is aware of appropriate hand washing in order to prevent cross contamination. Discussed with employee and PIC. COS.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed raw chicken to be thawing in a basin of water within the 3 compartment sink. Cease practice. Ensure proper thawing techniques: at refrigeration under 41 degrees F or under running water (below 70 degrees F in water temp) while completely submerged ensuring food does not exceed 41 degrees F in temperature. Discussed with multiple employees. Ensure proper thawing procedures. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

(REPEAT) Observed no sanitization bucket upon inspection. Facility was operational and cooking. Ensure a sani bucket is created and frequently changed throughout working hours in order to maintain the concentration of sanitizer. Sani bucket was created at request of Inspector. Bleach - 200 ppm. Discussed with PIC and multiple employees. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/1/22.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Baffles of the hood system have accumulation of grease and debris. Steam Power comes 3x yearly. Wash baffles in between professional services to hinder build-up.
2. Fryers are heavily coated in grease debris on the sides and interior doors. Drain the fryers of oil and clean the equipment.
3. The floor beneath the fryers and oven/grill prep line have a significant amount of grease, food splash, dirty rags, and debris under the entire area. Pull all equipment and clean the area - floors, walls, equipment. The prep line is in need of deep cleaning.
4. Dust is present on the vent grates above the soda machine in the front serving area. Clean the vent.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. A schedule should be created for the prep line in order to address item #3 in this violation. A schedule would be beneficial for not only routine cleaning of the floors, walls, and equipment, but also to hinder any pests that may be attracted to the area. Clean areas before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed raw chicken to be stored above raw pork within the walk-in cooler shelf. Chicken should be at the bottom of the shelving and pork should be above the raw chicken. Storage order signage is posted on the walk-in cooler door. Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff is aware of appropriate storage order of foods. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

(REPEAT) Observed no bleach to be pulling into the dish machine. Multiple attempts were conducted and checked with test strips - 0 ppm. PIC called service company during the inspection and repairs were being conducted. MJ Kellner changed the line for the bleach on the machine. Corrected - 200 ppm. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/21/21.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed several in-use rags in kitchen. No sanitization bucket was present upon inspection. Ensure rags are stored in sanitizer buckets in between uses. Ensure the sani buckets have appropriate concentration of sanitizer and frequent changes are conducted to keep sanitization levels accurate. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple buckets of spatulas, ladles, and egg beaters near the two reach-in freezers in the kitchen to have the food-contact side of the instrument facing upright out of the bucket. Reverse - ensure the food contact side is inside the buckets in order to be able to grab the utensils with the handle side. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed a piece of Nudo board type material to be missing on the interior frame of the walk-in cooler door. Replace piece of board so the area is smooth and easily cleanable. Caulk the piece on the door if needed. Discussed repairs with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no sanitization bucket upon inspection. Facility was operational and cooking. Ensure a sani bucket is created and frequently changed throughout working hours in order to maintain the concentration of sanitizer. Sani bucket was created at request of Inspector. Bleach - 200 ppm. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed no bleach to be pulling into the dish machine. Multiple attempts were conducted. Inspector utilized her own test strips and facility test strips - 0 ppm. PIC is calling service company. Due to the holiday, the follow-up is scheduled for 12/27/21. Facility will be closed for the holidays. Inspector instructed facility to utilize the 3 compartment sink until it is repaired. Facility has bleach for food-contact surfaces and is an approved brand.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple food items in the walk-in cooler to be out of date. Items were voluntarily discarded. Date marking of within 7 day foods was missing for some items as well. Ensure disposition of foods past 7 day date marking is habitual. Ensure date marking on all prepared and/or thawed foods. Discussed with PIC. Facility has actively improved on date marking and disposition and the issues today were minor as compared to previous inspections. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 3/12/20 and 8/4/21.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed walk-in cooler to have part coming away from the door. Ensure door is fixed so it is flush and smooth. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple items in the kitchen refrigerator and the walk-in cooler that were beyond the 7 day date marking and needed discarded:
1. Kitchen Refrigerator: leftover gumbo, egg washes
2. Walk-In Cooler: coleslaw mix, muffins, cut melons, baked chicken bbq pork, cooked pork

Ensure routine checking of cooler and discarding of foods beyond the 7 day date marking. Foods were voluntarily discarded. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/12/20.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed caulking of the 3 compartment sink to be missing and/or peeling away from the wall and the sink. Ensure repairs (re-caulking) before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

(REPEAT) Observed mop to be hanging in a manner that does not allow drip and/or air drying. Discussed with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 3/10/20 and 11/8/19.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-202.11: Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas. \

Observed a missing light shield in the kitchen above the 3 compartment sink. Ensure lights are protected within the kitchen and food preparation areas. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(2) (Pf) PIC does not demonstrate the responsibility of preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by employees that may cause food borne disease. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(2).

Observed facility to lack signed employee health reporting agreements. Discussed importance of document and need to review with all food handlers. Provided additional employee health reporting agreement paper. Inspector will follow-up regarding signatures on 3/20/20.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11  (C) Employee observed drinking from an uncovered cup in the food preparation area. Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups. Reference 2-401.11.

Observed an uncovered employee drink in the kitchen area. Please ensure employee drinks have a lid and straw and placed in a designated area of the kitchen. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

Observed multiple employees to improperly wash hands. Employees did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. After properly washing hands with soap and warm water, food handlers should dry hands with paper towels and then turn faucet off with a barrier such as the paper towel just used as to not cross-contaminate. Discussed proper hand washing technique with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11  (P) Salad stored in the kitchen refrigerator is spoiled. All foods intended for consumption must be in safe and unadulterated condition. Reference 3-101.11.

Observed a bag of salad to be noticably spoiled. Discussed discarding foods after 7 days of date marking. Salad was voluntarily discarded. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 11/8/19. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Ice machine (food contact surface) is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed interior of ice machine to have a build-up of mold. Discussed routine cleaning of the ice machine with PIC. Ice machine is a food contact surface and should be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Inspector will follow-up on 3/20/20.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple food items throughout facility. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed multiple food items throughout facility to lack date marking. The refrigerator within the kitchen had many items without a date including opened bacon, prepared coleslaw, prepared gravy, opened sausage, bags of open shred cheese, thawed fish, and cut lemons. The walk-in cooler had multiple items without a date, as well. Items included prepared chicken, opened milk gallon jug, prepared potatoes, and defrosted ground beef and meats. Discussed date marking with PIC and importance of procedures. Employess date marked the items during inspection. Provided date marking paperwork. COS.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date of ham and shred cheese exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed sliced ham to have a date mark of 3/2/20 which is over the 7 day time limit. Multiple shred cheese bags were open but lacked date marking. Employee voluntarily discarded ham and shred cheese. Discussed discarding foods with date marking that exceeds 7 days. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112  (C) A thermometer is not provided in the refrigerator. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112.

Observed refrigerator in kitchen to lack a thermometer. Other cold holding units were stocked with thermometers. Ensure this refrigerator has a thermometer placed within in by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text:
3-302.12  (C) Food storage containers are not labeled. Identify food storage containers with common name of the food. Reference 3-302.12.

Observed the bulk flour and sugar containers to lack common names. Discussed need for common names on all food items removed from original packaging. Employee utilized inspector's sharpie and placed common names on storage bins. COS.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination at walk-in cooler. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

Observed cardboard box of bacon within walk-in cooler to be storing bacon directly in contact with the cardboard. Bacon should have wax lining within box and wax paper around each layer/sheet that separates bacon. Discussed proper bacon storage with PIC. COS. See attached photo in CDP.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

Observed multiple in-use wiping rags throughout facility to not be placed within sanitization buckets. Discussed need for in-use rags to be held within sanitization of correct concentrations during all times rags are not being used. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 11/8/19.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination at multiple areas of facility. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

Observed multiple areas of facility to not have clean utensils protected from contamination:
1. Handles of flour and sugar scoops were within the food items in the storage bins. Discussed keeping the handle out of the foods with PIC. COS.
2. Clean utensils were observed within the storage cup to have the food contact side upright and making it difficult to take utensil out without touching food contact side. Discussed reversing the way the utensils are stored in order to hinder cross-contamination. 
3. Single-use utensils were observed to be stored in various directions at storage bin. Ensure the single-use utensils are aligned in one direction in order to hinder cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text:
4-901.11  (C) Equipment/Utensils are not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.

Observed multiple stacked cups near soda machine to be stacked without completely air drying after being cleaned and sanitized. Discussed need to have cups completely dry before stacking. Cease practice.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on multiple areas of facility. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed multiple areas of facility to have nonfood-contact surfaces that were not clean. Areas included:
1. Exterior of dish machine observed to have heavy accumulation of food debris.
2. Various reach-in freezers and the refridgerator observed to have food debris on shelving units. Ensure routine cleaning of the cold holding units.
3. Plastic liners on wire tiered metal shelving units of dry storage area observed to have debris.
4. Handles of unused hot holding unit (used as dry storage) and handles of cold holding units observed with debris.
5. Fan of soda machine observed with dust accumulation. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 11/8/19.
6. Hot holding water observed to have debris within.  

Ensure routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces occurs frequently. Wash, rinse, sanitize areas before next routine insepction, as well as needed.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop to be stored incorrectly in-between uses. Mops should be hung in a manner that allows to drip dry and/or air dry. Discussed proper practice with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 11/8/19. COS.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Coving was found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed missing coving in the men's bathroom. Discussed need for coving so the wall and floor and smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure coving is placed in area before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-202.11  (C) Lighting was found not shielded or otherwise protected in the walk-in cooler area. Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens; or unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Reference 6-202.11.

Observed light shielf in walk-in cooler to be broken and cracked. Discussed replacing light shield with PIC.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11  (P) Tomatoes stored in the walk-in fridge are spoiled. All foods intended for consumption must be in safe and unadulterated condition. Reference 3-101.11.

Observed tomatoes that are spoiled within the walk-in fridge. Discussed with PIC and discarded. This is a repeat violation for the 2019 inspection year.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 50 ppm at three compartment sink. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed concentration of of quat in 3 compartment sink to be low: 50 ppm. Discussed with PIC and added more quat to the sink.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The following food contact surfaces were soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris: serving spoon and can opener. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed serving spoon to be soiled with debris. Discussed with PIC and removed from service.

findings.comment: Wall at back door jamb is missing a trim piece and nudo material is not sealed. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings. Seal this area.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
There was a can of pickled beets that was badly dented on the bottom seam.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.
The can of beets was discarded to CORRECT THE VIOLATION.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Bulk bins of white powders (flour and sugar?) were not labeled.  Make sure white powders are always labeled.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
There were several small containers of potentially hazardous food in the walk-in freezer that were beyond the 7 day use-by date.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
The food was discarded to CORRECT the violation.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Beef knuckles and other raw beef products were stored above fish and greens in left vertical freezer (all foods were frozen).  IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED - freezer was immediately re-arranged so food was stored properly.  Proper Freezer/Cold Storage hand-out was left with establishment.
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Scoops in white powder bins (flour and sugar?) had fallen into the food, handles too.  IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED - scoops were righted so handles were facing up.  Make sure handles are always straight up to minimize hand-to-food contact.
750-280  All food handling utensils shall be properly stored:  handle extended out of food; clean and dry; or in running potable water dipping wells.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
A dumpster lid was open.
750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.
Close the dumpster lid.

findings.title: Outside storage area clean, enclosure properly constructed
findings.comment:
There is refuse on the dumpster pad behind the dumpster and grease receptacle.
750-1140c Outside storage areas shall be large enough to store the outside garbage and refuse containers and shall be kept clean.
Clean the dumpster pad.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Floor under orange counter is soiled, especially as floor gets closer to wall.  Thoroughly clean floor under the counter top, all the way to the wall.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Walk-in cooler at 55 F and items inside are at 50 F.  At start of inspection, unit was about 50 F and items inside were 41-43 F.  The temperature was checked again at end of inspection and it went up, but the door had been open often during lunch prep.  The temperature gauge was turned down and the door will kept shut as much as possible to get the temperature down.  Inspector will return later today to check temperature of WIC and food inside.  In the meantime, the temperature will be monitored by staff to make sure it is coming down to 41 F or food will be removed and stored in unit holding at 41 F or less.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Walk-in cooler at 55 F, but at start of inspection it was at 50 F and food was about 41-43 F inside.  Unit was turned down and temperature will be monitored by staff to reach 41 F or less.  Move food out of unit if the temperature is not coming down rapidly to avoid spoilage.  Inspector will return later today to check temperature and discard food if necessary.
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed chicken, fish, and shrimp to be thawing in containers of water.  Thawing shall be done under running water, in the cooler, or as part of the cooking process.  All of these food items were being cooked within the hour.
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Observed two rotten apples stored in a drawer in the walk-in cooler where other foods were stored.  The two rotten apples were discarded during the inspection.  *Violation Corrected*
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the guard on the slicer to be soiled.  Clean and sanitize the slicer and guard to remove food debris.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
The scoop handle in the sugar was stored down in the sugar. Keep and handles sticking up while in storage.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Clean cups were stored on the top shelf in dry storage uncovered. Cover or store the cups inverted.
750-850  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
The women's restroom does not have a covered waste can. Place a covered waste can in the women's restroom.
750-1110d Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
The hand sinks in the men's and women's restrooms were not caulked to the wall.  Caulk the hand sinks to the wall.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Mold was observed in the ice machine deflector.  Wash and sanitize the ice deflector.
750-800d The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750.120a: Observed a container of cooked neck bones to be dated "4-9", which is over the 7 day limit to keep prepared foods by 3 days.  Potentially Hazardous Foods (PHFs) prepared by facility shall be dated and can be kept for a maximum of 7 days.  The neck bones were discarded.  *Violation Corrected*

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750.690: Observed duct tape on the outside of the white microwave in the kitchen and on the freezer part of the small cooler located next to the grill.  Remove duct tape so that surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750.1210a: Ceiling tiles in the restrooms and above the serving area in the front are acoustic tiles (except for a couple that have been recently replaced).  At the next remodel of facility, replace the ceiling tiles with tiles that are smooth and easily cleanable, like the new tiles that were recently added.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed the absence of a label on containers storing bulk dry goods. Place a label on the outside of containers storing bulk dry goods.

Absence of a label on container storing small individual dressing cups or each dressing cups. Place a label on container of dressing cups with date of preparation or date to discard.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed a couple plastic storage containers, storing food, to have broken or cracked lids. Replace the broken lids. Food contact surfaces shall be free from cracks and crevices.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed a small area on wall on left side of 3 compartment sink to be in disrepair. Repair the wall so it is smooth and easily cleanable.

Ceiling tiles in restrooms and above serving line/front service area are acoustic tiles. At next remodel, replace ceiling tiles with tiles that are smooth and easily cleanable.
